Item 5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers.


On November 11, 2026, the Board of Directors, or the Board, of NVIDIA Corporation accepted the resignation of Jen-Hsun Huang, as NVIDIA’s President, Chief Executive Officer and member of the Board, effective immediately.


Following Mr. Huang’s resignation, the Board appointed NVIDIA’s Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette M. Kress, age 59, to serve as interim Chief Executive Officer, while the Board conducts a search for a new Chief Executive Officer. Ms. Kress has served as NVIDIA’s Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since 2013 and will continue in that role while she serves as the interim Chief Executive Officer.


On November 11, 2026, the Board appointed Harvey C. Jones, age 73, as Chair of the Board. Mr. Jones has served on the Board since 1993. He has been the Managing Partner of Square Wave Ventures, a private family office, since 2004 and has over 30 years of experience as an entrepreneur, high technology executive, and venture investor.

NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition


•Jensen Huang Resigns
•Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Appointed Interim CEO
•Harvey C. Jones Appointed First-Ever Chair of the Board


SANTA CLARA, Calif., November 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately.
 
Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates.


Kress has served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA since joining the company in September 2013. During her tenure, she has led the company’s finance organization and has played a key role in NVIDIA’s growth and evolution. Prior to joining NVIDIA, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft.


The Board of Directors appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever Chair of the Board.  Mr. Jones has been an entrepreneur, technology executive, and active venture investor for over 30 years, including serving as Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of Synopsys.


“Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” said Harvey Jones, Chair of the NVIDIA Board of Directors. “She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing NVIDIA’s strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.”  
“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Colette Kress, Interim CEO and CFO, NVIDIA. “We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.” 


Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.


NVIDIA will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results on Tuesday, November 17, at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT, as previously scheduled, followed by its earnings call at 2 p.m. PT.

Statement From NVIDIA Board of Directors
November 8, 2026

The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.  

The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.

While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. 

Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.

The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.

A Message to Our Company
NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang sent the following email to NVIDIA employees earlier today.
November 8, 2026

I owe my family and all of you an apology.

I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.

Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.

To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust. 

To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.

Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.

My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy.

Jensen

PYC

At the invitation of the government of the Republic of Senegal, President Xi Jinping’s Special Envoy and Director of China’s General Administration of Sport Gao Zhidan will attend the opening ceremony of the fourth Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal on October 31.

At the invitation of Premier of the State Council Li Qiang, Federal Chancellor Christian Stocker of Austria will pay an official visit to China from November 2 to 7.

CCTV: The Chinese side has announced that Sultan Haitham of Oman will pay a state visit to China. Could you share the program of the visit? How does China view the current state of bilateral relations? What are your expectations for the visit?

Guo Jiakun: This will be the first visit to China by Sultan Haitham since ascending to the throne and by an Omani head of state since diplomatic ties were established 48 years ago. As such, it is of great significance for advancing bilateral relations. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will hold talks with Sultan Haitham to have an in-depth exchange of view on China-Oman relations and issues of mutual interest. There will also be a meeting with Premier Li Qiang.

China and Oman enjoy a profound traditional friendship. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of President Xi and Sultan Haitham, our two countries have seen deepening political mutual trust, steady progress in mutually beneficial cooperation, increasingly close people-to-people and cultural exchanges, and good communication in international and regional issues. We hope to work together with the Omani side to take the upcoming visit as an opportunity to bring our strategic partnership to new heights.

China News Service: We notice that the Committee on Disarmament and International Security (First Committee) of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly approved resolutions on “Further practical measures for the prevention of an arms race in outer space” and “No first placement of weapons in outer space.” The vision of a community with a shared future for humanity was again included in the resolutions. Could you share more details?

Guo Jiakun: China advocates the peaceful use and safety of outer space, and promotes the building of a community with a shared future for humanity in the domain of outer space. Since 2017, China has, together with relevant countries, jointly submitted to the First Committee of the UN General Assembly each year the two resolutions on “Further practical measures for the prevention of an arms race in outer space” and “No first placement of weapons in outer space.” China firmly opposes the weaponization of and any arms race in outer space, and calls for negotiations on an international legal instrument to safeguard lasting peace and common security and build a community with a shared future for humanity in the domain of outer space. 

The First Committee of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly once again adopted the above resolutions by a majority. This marks the tenth consecutive year that the vision of a community with a shared future for humanity has been incorporated into UNGA resolutions on outer space. It fully demonstrates that the vision conforms to the trend of the times and meets the common expectations of the international community, and has become an international public good of major significance in today’s world. The recently released China’s Position on Strengthening Outer Space Governance is consistent with this vision. China stands ready to work with the international community to jointly build a peaceful, secure, open and cooperative outer space, and to ensure that the outcomes of outer space exploration benefit all humanity.

AFP: The New York Times had an exclusive report about how a Chinese businesswoman, who was close to NVIDIA Chief Jensen Huang, was found to be giving intelligence to Beijing. This is according to intelligence from American spy agencies. Is China aware of this report, and do you have a comment on this?

Guo Jiakun: Relevant report is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China. 

People’s Daily: China just announced the upcoming visit of Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker. Could you please share more information about the program? How does China see the current China-Austria relations and what’s China’s expectation for the visit?

Guo Jiakun: This will be Chancellor Stocker’s first visit to China since taking office, and the first visit by an Austrian chancellor to China in seven years. Chancellor Stocker will first land in Shanghai, where he will attend the ninth China International Import Expo. During his stay in Beijing, President Xi Jinping will meet with Chancellor Stocker, and Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji will hold talks and meet with him respectively.

Austria is a friendly strategic partner of China in Europe. This year marks the 55th anniversary of our diplomatic relations. At present, the two countries enjoy sound momentum of growth in bilateral ties, with close high-level interactions and ever-deepening exchanges and cooperation in various fields. As the two countries mark the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations, China stands ready to work with Austria to deepen political mutual trust, strengthen mutually beneficial cooperation and carry forward our traditional friendship based on mutual respect and equality, so as to deliver more practical outcomes in bilateral ties and help stabilize and improve China-Europe economic and trade relations at an early date. 

CCTV: The G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting will be held in Atlanta, the U.S. South Africa, a founding member of the G20, was once again not invited. What’s your comment? 

Guo Jiakun: As a major platform for international economic cooperation, the G20 plays an important role in strengthening multilateralism, promoting world economic growth, and improving global governance. South Africa is an important member of the G20. China supports South Africa in continuing its participation in G20 activities.

AFP: The Swiss President Guy Parmelin will meet with President Xi Jinping. Following the meeting, both countries will sign an optimized bilateral free trade agreement. Can China share the expectations you have for this upgraded agreement?

Guo Jiakun: We’ve shared information on President Parmelin’s visit to China. There will be timely updates on the visit. Please stay tuned.

Reuters: We had a story out of Washington that U.S. telecom regulator is voting next month to ban Chinese telecom companies from direct access to U.S. telephone numbers. And also the same U.S. regulator has decided to ban all Chinese labs from testing U.S. electronics like smartphones. Any comment regarding those matters?

Guo Jiakun: The U.S. is overstretching the concept of national security and abusing state power to go after Chinese businesses. China firmly opposes and deplores this. The U.S. move severely hinders normal economic and trade cooperation between Chinese and American businesses and is not in the interest of any party including US companies and consumers. China will do what is necessary to firmly defend its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.

Special Envoy of the Communist Party of Cuba (PCC) and the Cuban Government, Member of the Political Bureau of the PCC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla will pay an official visit to China from November 10 to 13.

At the invitation of Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, Slovakia’s Minister of Foreign and European Affairs Juraj Blanár will visit China from November 10 to 11.

Xinhua News Agency: According to reports, a Pakistani astronaut will join the Shenzhou XXIV mission crew as payload specialist and complete a short orbital flight before returning to Earth with the Shenzhou XXIII spaceship. I wonder if you have any comment on this?

Guo Jiakun: Exploration of the vast universe and peaceful use of outer space are humanity’s shared pursuit and bear on the welfare of all peoples. China advocates the peaceful use of outer space, engages in active international space cooperation, and promotes the building of a community with a shared future in the domain of outer space.

China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners. Having the Pakistani astronaut on board China’s spaceships will mark the first ever joint mission of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China’s manned space program. The Pakistani astronaut will be the first foreign astronaut to step into China’s space station. This is yet another key outcome of bilateral cooperation as we mark the 75th anniversary of China-Pakistan diplomatic ties. We stand ready to work with the Pakistani side to carry forward our traditional friendship, deepen cooperation in space and other fields, and bring bilateral relations to new heights.

CCTV: Can you provide more details about the visit by Special Envoy of the PCC and Government of Cuba, Member of the Political Bureau of the PCC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla?

Guo Jiakun: China and Cuba are good friends, good comrades and good brothers. The upcoming visit by Special Envoy Rodríguez speaks volumes about the high political mutual trust between our two countries. China attaches great importance to this visit. We look forward to an in-depth exchange of views on China-Cuba relations and issues of mutual interest, and will work with the Cuban side to further implement the important common understandings reached between our two leaders, strengthen communication and coordination, deepen exchanges and cooperation across the board, and continue building a China-Cuba community with a shared future. 

AFP: Chip giant NVIDIA’s board has opened a probe into Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman U.S. officials say was working for Chinese intelligence. This comes after reports from The New York Times and the Financial Times linking Jensen Huang to a Chinese citizen and tech executive. Can the Chinese foreign ministry comment on this? (Similar question from NBC)

Guo Jiakun: We responded to that last week. The “Chinese spy” allegation is purely unsubstantiated and directed at smearing China.

Beijing Youth Daily: To follow up on the announcement of Slovak Foreign Minister Blanár’s visit to China, how does China view its relations with Slovakia? What’s China’s expectation of this visit?

Guo Jiakun: China and Slovakia enjoy traditional friendship. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of the leaders of the two countries, China-Slovakia relations have made marked progress. In particular, since China-Slovakia strategic partnership was established in 2024, solid progress has been made in deepening exchanges and cooperation in various fields. In July this year, Slovak President Pellegrini paid a state visit to China. President Xi Jinping held talks with him to jointly draw a blueprint for the future development of bilateral relations. China will work with Slovakia to carry forward traditional friendship, deepen political mutual trust, expand practical cooperation, strive for solid progress in advancing high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and cooperation between China and Central and Eastern European countries, and sustain the strong momentum of bilateral relations.

AFP: U.S. President Donald Trump said he would likely be meeting with the leaders of Russia and China next week in Shenzhen to discuss ending the Iran war as well as other topics like denuclearization. Can the foreign ministry comment on this or offer us any additional details on the agenda of the meeting with Trump and Putin?

Guo Jiakun: China maintains communication with the relevant parties on the meeting between the three presidents. As for your specific question, I have no information to offer at the moment.

CGTN: Austrian Federal Chancellor Christian Stocker recently paid an official visit to China. How does China see the outcomes of the visit and how do you envision the future development of China-Austria relations?

Guo Jiakun: This year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Austria. As a highlight in the commemoration program, Federal Chancellor Christian Stocker paid a successful visit to China and attended the ninth China International Import Expo. During Chancellor Stocker’s stay in Beijing, President Xi Jinping met with him and Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji held talks and met with him respectively. 

The leaders had in-depth exchanges of views on bilateral ties and China-EU relations as well as international and regional issues of mutual interest. Both sides agreed to carry forward the traditional friendship between the two countries, respect each other’s core interests, sustain the positive momentum in high-level exchanges, deepen mutually beneficial practical cooperation in such fields as economy, trade, culture, science and technology and at the sub-national level on the basis of mutual trust, and strengthen coordination at the UN Security Council and other multilateral platforms to jointly support multilateralism.

During the visit, Premier Li and Chancellor Stocker witnessed the signing of three documents on cooperation in economy, trade, social security and other areas, which serves to consolidate the foundation of bilateral ties and illustrate what can be achieved if China and the EU see each other as partners and tap into the potential for cooperation.

The Paper: We noticed that the Standing Committee of the 14th National People’s Congress decided at its 25th Meeting to ratify the Agreement on the Establishment of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO). Could you share more information on that?

Guo Jiakun: In July this year, at the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance, President Xi Jinping announced that WAICO had come into being. The initiative has received positive response from the international community, with 38 countries as the founding members.

As the initiator and the host country of WAICO, China is now taking the lead to ratify the Agreement on the Establishment of WAICO. That demonstrates China’s genuine aspiration and firm commitment to getting the organization up and running. Guided by the vision of extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit, China will make continuous efforts to promote the physical operation of WAICO, and focus on the practical cooperation and capacity building in the Global South, so that all countries can share the opportunities and dividends brought by AI. We welcome and expect more countries to join WAICO, to promote global AI development for good and for all, and to jointly build a just and equitable global AI governance system.

AFP: Reuters reported that about 600,000 of NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips are stored in Hong Kong. The chips are awaiting shipment to mainland China as Beijing withholds approval for large scale imports despite demand from tech firms. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this report?

Guo Jiakun: China’s position on the U.S. export of chips to China is consistent. For anything specific, I’d refer you to competent authorities.

RIA Novosti: Earlier, Washington Post columnist David Ignatius reported citing sources, that the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump has asked China to help bring an end to the conflict with Iran. Could you please confirm this?

Guo Jiakun: To prolong the conflict between the U.S. and Iran does not serve the common interest of the parties concerned and the international community. Relevant parties should stick to peace, resolve disputes through dialogue and negotiation, and restore peace and tranquility in the Middle East and Gulf region at an early date.

Bloomberg: Jensen Huang has been an advocate for looser policy and selling more chips to China. And the Democrats have also just won the Congress and may have a different approach to tech curbs. How will China respond if the U.S. pushes for tighter tech curbs, including on chips?

Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigns, chipmaker names CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO
Ram Iyer
Julie Bort
6:10 AM PST · November 12, 2026
IMAGE CREDITS:
DAVID PAUL MORRIS/BLOOMBERG / GETTY IMAGES

Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as president and chief executive of Nvidia, the company said on Thursday, just a few days after he admitted to a romantic affair with an alleged Chinese spy, sparking a U.S. national security crisis.

In a regulatory filing, Nvidia said its board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday.

Nvidia said its current chief financial officer and executive vice president, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO until the company finds a permanent successor. Kress will continue to serve as the company’s CFO.

Nvidia’s shares were down nearly 12% in early morning trading on Thursday. Since Friday, the company’s stock has fallen by as much as 19%, resulting in a market cap loss of more than $855 billion.

Huang founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it as CEO ever since. Under his leadership, Nvidia played a crucial role in developing the graphics processing unit (GPU), a specialized chip that does graphics processing for PCs, as we know it today. The chips were not an immediate hit, and the early days of Nvidia were characterized by struggle and layoffs, but eventually, it struck on a GPU design that performed so well, it became the standard for graphics processing.

These chips also turned out to be extremely good at doing large numbers of calculations simultaneously, which has made them popular for computation-intensive tasks like crypto mining, and more recently, training and running neural networks, which are what AI models are at their core.

Nvidia was initially focused on making GPUs aimed at gaming, but it had already moved into general-purpose computing by 2006 with the launch of the CUDA architecture, which lets developers use the chips for other tasks, such as doing calculations and research. After AI researchers began using the company’s GPUs to train neural networks over a decade ago, Huang leaned in toward developing chips for AI and then data centers, and grew it from there into its dominant position.

Under Huang, the company has been by far the biggest beneficiary of the AI industry’s skyrocketing growth, which has largely depended on Nvidia’s GPUs for training and running large language models. Before ChatGPT launched and sparked the AI boom, Nvidia shares were trading at about $15. As of last month, they had risen more than 1,450% to an all-time high of $243. Its market cap consequently has also risen by an eye-watering $5.5 trillion since then, reaching as high as $5.88 trillion early in October.

Revenue, of course, has also ballooned, rising more than 1,500% to $96.22 billion as of the company’s second quarter, from $5.93 billion in Q3 2023, right before the ChatGPT moment. Profits increased nearly 88 times in that period to $59.69 billion as of July 2026, from $680 million in October 2023.

That success was predicated on large part by the AI industry’s continued development, which Huang seemingly made his personal mission. He traveled to conferences and events around the world to promote his products and AI, lobbied extensively for looser regulation after the Biden administration placed export controls on the sale of high-power AI chips to China, and cultivated a close relationship with Trump, often to Nvidia’s benefit.

The resignation and controversy come at a crucial moment for Nvidia. China was always a big market for the company, though its impact on the company’s finances has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives. Chinese customers accounted for revenue of about $7.9 billion in the company’s second quarter, roughly 8% of total revenue.

Repercussions galore

The potential implications of Huang’s departure for the AI and data center industries are vast, given how active Huang, and by extension Nvidia, has been in furthering the AI boom. In particular, it raises questions about the future of Nvidia’s sprawling AI investments, which have helped bankroll everything from startups developing new technologies to the enormous data centers needed to run them.

Under Huang, Nvidia deftly used its financial muscle to support companies buying its chips, effectively helping to finance the market for its own products, as well as lobbying Washington to relax potential rules around AI and data center regulation.

As of the end of its second quarter, Nvidia reported $99 billion worth of investments and another $25 billion of commitments. It also has $36 billion in cloud service commitments, which are arrangements that help AI cloud operators finance the GPUs and data center equipment they buy from Nvidia, with the chipmaker saying it will buy compute from them and potentially earn a share of their operators’ revenue.

Nvidia has also been investing directly in neoclouds, the companies serving a lot of the AI processing needs. In January, the company invested $2 billion in CoreWeave, and another $2 billion in Nebius in March. The chipmaker was said to be considering being a guarantor for Nscale’s planned West Virginia data center project. It’s also signed up to provide up to $105 billion worth of credit guarantees for an OpenAI data center campus in Ohio.

Nvidia’s also a major investor in the labs building the AI models that run on its GPUs, putting $30 billion into OpenAI, and $10 billion into Anthropic. It’s also backed Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab as part of a deal involving at least 1 GW of its Vera Rubin GPU systems. The chipmaker has also invested $3.5 billion in MediaTek to help the Taiwanese company develop custom AI chips that work with Nvidia’s systems.

Many investors have grown uneasy with the enormous amounts of debt companies in the space were raising to sustain the AI infrastructure buildout, and Huang’s exit throws another uncertainty-shaped wrench into the works. CoreWeave’s shares were down about 9% on Thursday, reversing part of a 25% rally on Wednesday, while Nebius is down about 16%. IREN fell 6.6%.

Nvidia’s board has also appointed Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993. As chair, Jones is likely to play a central role in Nvidia’s search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang.

Huang is the single largest personal shareholder at Nvidia, but he owns only about 3.5% of the company’s shares. Unlike many of Silicon Valley’s tech giants, he does not hold supervoting rights, and the board had the power to vote him out at any time.

Huang famously ran a very flat organization, with around 60 direct reports. There was no heir apparent or succession plan either (although two of his children also worked in executive roles at the company). Huang famously maintained tight control over the company he founded, making it challenging for Nvidia to find a path forward without him.

The industry will get its first glimpse of that next week during the quarterly conference call. Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday.

“Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” the company said in a statement.

Note: This story was updated to add details about Nvidia’s growth and Huang’s efforts to promote AI development, as well as its focus on China.

The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
Amanda Silberling
7:58 AM PST · November 13, 2026

Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.

The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.

The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

November 13, 2026: Huang was not confident in his successor, Colette Kress; reports describe Huang as ‘broken’

More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia.

Bloomberg reported that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”

Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had been critical of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is said to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making.

November 12, 2026: Democrats launch investigation into Nvidia; Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick summoned to testify before Senate Banking Committee

In a scathing letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) said they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy.

“Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.

That same evening, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) requested that Huang and Lutnick both testify before the Senate Banking Committee.

“The American people deserve answers,” Scott wrote on X.

November 12, 2026: Huang was having a third affair with another Nvidia employee, according to Reuters

After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.

November 12, 2026: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress named as interim CEO; Huang agrees to testify before Congress

Nvidia said its board had accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.

Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.

Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.

“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”

The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.

November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang

After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.

Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said. The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.

November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says

The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.

According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.

November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair

Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.

November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements

The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.

November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy

Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.

Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.

In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.  

November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”

On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.

“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.

When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”

November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation

Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.

“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”

“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.

Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.

November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing

Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.

“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote.

Megaspeed's vacant offices raise questions about ties to Nvidia and China
By Isabel Vincent

Updated on: November 13, 2026 / 10:19 AM EST / CBS News

Add CBS News on Google

The unusual global footprint of Megaspeed International, the Singapore-based company at the center of the Nvidia Chinese spy scandal, is fueling questions about whether it's a front for the Chinese government.

One of Megaspeed's leaders is Alice Huang, the woman with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was having an affair, and who is suspected by U.S. intelligence of being an asset of China's Ministry of State Security. On Thursday, Jensen Huang resigned.

In the past three years, Megaspeed, formerly a gaming company, has been one of Nvidia's biggest foreign customers, purchasing nearly $5 billion in AI chips and advanced hardware, The New York Times first reported. 

And yet Megaspeed's corporate headquarters sat practically empty, according to The Straits Times, an English-language newspaper in Singapore. Questions have also been raised about its outposts in Australia and Malaysia.

Published reports in recent days revealed that the company listed a newspaper vendor as the director of its Australian subsidiary, and one of its Malaysia offices consisted of a dilapidated storefront outside Kuala Lumpur. Yet another Malaysia office was tucked into a shopping mall. 

Megaspeed began as an offshoot of a China-based gaming firm and grew into a juggernaut by gaining access to restricted Nvidia AI computer chips. U.S. investigators say that Alice Huang used her contacts in the industry and a series of shell companies to gain access to 240,000 chips banned for export into China. Now it is being probed in both the U.S. and Singapore for allegedly smuggling those chips into China. 

In a statement Thursday, Megaspeed said it "takes its compliance obligations under U.S. export control laws extremely seriously" and that it's "committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government."

The company also said that it "has cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and stands ready to cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority."

President Trump said this week the FBI is also investigating romantic and business ties between Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang and Alice Huang (who are not related). 

Earlier this week, Jensen Huang, who is married, apologized for the affair in a statement to Nvidia's employees. The company launched an independent investigation of the matter, and an Nvidia shareholder filed a class action lawsuit Tuesday alleging that Huang concealed a relationship with Alice Huang and misled shareholders about national security concerns raised by the relationship. 

Nvidia's board said Sunday that it had no reason to believe that the company's secrets or national security were compromised. "The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," its statement said.

However, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News on Wednesday that the board was preparing to oust Jensen Huang, a development that was first reported by the Wall Street Journal.

China expert Jacqueline Deal said that Nvidia's advanced AI chips could have ended up with the Chinese military. Deal, who is an adviser to State Armor, a nonprofit that studies global security threats, told CBS News, "If allegations are true, who will be fired? Nvidia has a compliance team that may have failed utterly." 

She also questioned the effectiveness of the U.S. Commerce Department, which has jurisdiction over export controls that may have been bypassed, potentially giving the Chinese military access to the world's most advanced chips.  

Here's what we now know about Megaspeed: 

It is a major Nvidia customer. Megaspeed and its Malaysian affiliate, Speedmatrix, purchased $4.8 billion of Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence equipment and processors over the last three years. 

In 2025, Megaspeed International faced an investigation by Singapore police for alleged breaches of local laws, but no details have emerged about the probe, according to The Straits Times.

The company grew rapidly. 

"Megaspeed International is a premier business partner of NVIDIA, strategically positioned in the Asia Pacific region," according to its LinkedIn profile, which claims it has between 201 and 500 employees. Three years ago it listed between two and 10 employees, according to the South China Morning Post. 

Megaspeed International did not reply to a request for comment. It posted an "official statement" on its website addressing what it called "misleading information" and "incorrect insinuations" accusing it of involvement in illegal chip transfers. 

"We want to be absolutely clear over the past six months our company has undergone multiple on-site inspections and reviews by key institutions, including the Bureau of Industry and Security of the US Commerce Department, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry of Malaysia and NVIDIA," said the message, which also appeared on the company's LinkedIn page. 

"These thorough investigations have confirmed that there has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities," the company said.

But in a statement on Thursday, the company said it had "retained a leading U.S. law firm to ... independently verify its export control compliance practices. Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws."  

Megaspeed was originally incorporated in 2015 under the name 7Road International, a subsidiary of a Chinese developer of popular video games and mobile apps based in Shenzhen, China, according to corporate filings.   

Huang Le Limited, a shell company in the British Virgin Islands, acquired 7Road International in March 2023. Huang Le is the Chinese name of Alice Huang. 

That same month, 7Road International was renamed Megaspeed International, and Huang became its managing director. The company also launched a subsidiary called Speedmatrix. 

By the end of October 2023, Huang and another Megaspeed director, Cang Yang, resigned from the company after it was bought up by a firm called Swiftdata, whose director is based in China, documents show.  

But there's some indication Huang may still be affiliated with the company. Culper Research, an activist short-selling firm, published a 40-page report on Nvidia in May that cited Megaspeed employees who said Huang was still running the company. 

The report also raised some concern about Jensen Huang's relationship with Megaspeed and Alice Huang, stating, "Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has not only vouched for Megaspeed, but seems to have quite literally walked alongside Megaspeed at every step, while maintaining an uncomfortably close relationship with Megaspeed's Alice Huang, a Chinese national."

Megaspeed lists its headquarters office address on the seventh floor of the Ocean Financial Centre in Singapore, a glass office tower in Singapore's central business district.  

When the Straits Times and The New York Times visited the Singapore offices around the same time late last year, they found little or no staff working. The Straits Times said the door was locked, and the Times found just two people in its office on a workday.

Megaspeed has an Australian subsidiary on the 10th floor of a commercial and retail tower in the heart of Sydney's central business district. Forty other businesses are on the same floor, and space in the building can be rented for as little as $17 per day, Australia's ABC News reported. Corporate filings name Shanghai-born Kai Kang, a 29-year-old newspaper vendor, as the director, according to Australian news reports. But Kang's newsstand is in Northern Victoria, over 400 miles from Sydney. Kang's father told Australia's ABC News this week that he had never heard of Megaspeed.

Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations he was target of Chinese intelligence effort
By Lucia I Suarez Sang, Kristin Brown

Updated on: November 9, 2026 / 8:04 PM EST / CBS News

Add CBS News on Google

Nvidia has launched an independent investigation of its co-founder and CEO, Jensen Huang, over allegations he was the target of an intelligence effort by China.

The allegations center around a Chinese business executive named Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence agencies believe was an asset of China's Ministry of State Security, the country's main intelligence agency.

The CIA, NSA and ODNI did not immediately respond to CBS News requests for comment.  

The New York Times reported last month that U.S. authorities were investigating Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen), a former executive of the Singapore-based Megaspeed, which buys AI chips from Nvidia. The report claims Jensen Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence officials believe was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security.

Two law enforcement sources confirmed to CBS News on Monday that the Justice Department's National Security Division is investigating Megaspeed. The investigation involves potential violations of U.S. export restrictions on advanced AI chips, the sources said.

In a message to Nvidia employees Sunday, Jensen Huang admitted, "I was unfaithful to my wife," and apologized for hurting her and their children, although he did not name the woman involved. "There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," he wrote.

"The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort," Nvidia's board of directors said in a statement Sunday. "A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation."

The board said it had no reason to believe that the company's secrets or national security were compromised.

"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," the statement said.

John Rizzo, a spokesperson for Nvidia, told CBS News on Sunday, "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the U.S. government would have notified us."

Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters Monday, "The so-called Chinese spy narrative is entirely baseless and constitutes slander and smear."

A company spokesperson said Jensen Huang "fully supports the review" and is committed to continuing to lead the company.

Jensen Huang said he had fallen short of his responsibilities to the company's employees, board and shareholders. He said he is "fully committed to NVIDIA" and will work to earn back their trust.

"Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation," he said in a statement. "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully."

"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American," he added.

Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years, according to The Times.

Asked about the report on Sunday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he couldn't comment, saying it was an "internal corporate matter."

On Monday, President Trump called Jensen Huang a "very high-quality person," saying during a White House briefing that "the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape." Mr. Trump also said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday to see how he was doing, and that Huang "said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy."

Nvidia, the world's most valuable company, has regularly surpassed Wall Street's earnings expectations in the past three years since its high-end chips emerged as AI's best building blocks. The Santa Clara, California-based company reported quarterly profits of $59.69 billion in August.

Nicole Sganga, Olivia Gazis and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Nvidia's stock slides as questions swirl around Jensen Huang's future as CEO
By Aimee Picchi

Updated on: November 9, 2026 / 4:21 PM EST / CBS News

Add CBS News on Google

Nvidia's stock price slid on Monday amid questions about CEO Jensen Huang's future at the chipmaker, following the board of directors' investigation into allegations that China targeted him in an intelligence operation.

The investigation is raising concerns about Huang's role at the company, which he co-founded and helped build into the world's second-most valuable company, with a $4.5 trillion valuation. Nvidia is barred from selling its high-end chips, specifically designed to power artificial intelligence models, to China due to competitive concerns.

Nvidia shares sank 4.3%, or $7.97, to $178.67, shrinking the chipmaker's market valuation by about $193 billion.

The allegations center around reports that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence officials believe was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, the country's main intelligence agency. On Sunday, Nvidia's board said it is starting an "independent investigation" into the allegations, sparking questions about the CEO's future with the company. 

"This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons," Dan Ives, a tech analyst at Yorkville Ives, said in a research note. "The key question investors will be asking is: Will Jensen remain CEO of Nvidia?"

Ives added, "There is clearly risk that Jensen could be removed as CEO depending on the board investigation, and this will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally."

In a statement to CBS News, an Nvidia spokesperson said that "Jensen is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption." The company didn't respond to a question about whether Huang had violated any of its corporate policies. 

The company's board said it had no reason to believe that the company's secrets or national security were compromised. John Rizzo, a spokesperson for Nvidia, told CBS News on Sunday, "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the U.S. government would have notified us."

The Chinese government dismissed allegations that it targeted Nvidia's chief executive, who co-founded the company in 1993, as part of an espionage operation. "The so-called Chinese spy narrative is entirely baseless and constitutes slander and smear," Guo Jiakun, a spokesperson for China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said in a statement. 

Who is Alice Huang?

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a former executive at a Singapore-based data center company, Megaspeed International, whose website touts its partnership with Nvidia.

Many offices in Singapore were closed on Monday for a holiday. Megaspeed and the Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

Succession challenges

Replacing Jensen Huang, 63, would prove challenging because he is viewed as integral to the company's success, tech analysts said on Monday. Huang also serves as the public face of Nvidia, appearing at industry events and media interviews in his trademark black leather jacket.

Huang is the company's fifth-largest shareholder, with about 3.4% of its shares, according to financial data provider FactSet.

"There is no known succession plan, and there is no leader in the company who would be the clear next step if he had to step down. In many ways, Jensen is Nvidia's Steve Jobs," said Daniel Newman, CEO of tech consulting firm Futurum, in an email.

He added, "That does not mean they cannot find a Tim Cook in the future, but it would be a massive changing of the guard, and the company has not been set up for that."

Another blow for the AI trade

The scandal puts more pressure on Nvidia shares, which have already been bruised by mounting investor concerns about the valuations of companies driving AI growth. Prior to Monday's early decline, Nvidia's shares had tumbled almost 20% over the last month amid a broader sell-off in AI stocks. 

The board investigation into Huang could loom over Nvidia and raise the risk that U.S. regulators could impose additional restrictions on the company's chip exports, according to Adam Crisafulli, an analyst at Vital Knowledge.

"The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised," said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy.

In recent years, Jensen Huang has lobbied federal authorities to loosen limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China, winning approval from President Trump to sell its H200 chips this year. Those chips are not Nvidia's most advanced models, but they are still considered important products for Nvidia. 

Previously, Huang also lobbied Mr. Trump to be allowed to sell Nvidia's less-advanced H20 chips, which were designed to comply with U.S. export restrictions on China.

"The real potential fallout from the Jensen Huang scandal will be the U.S. government imposing dramatically more draconian restrictions on sales of sophisticated chips to China (the issue isn't the H200 but instead the fact that a large amount of higher-end Nvidia products are still making it into the hands of Chinese buyers)," Crisafulli said in a research note.

By Mithil Aggarwal

HONG KONG — Megaspeed, the tech company at the center of the Chinese spy scandal that engulfed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said Thursday it will cooperate with the U.S. government’s investigations into the matter.

Megaspeed’s statement came hours before the resignation of Huang, one of the leaders of the AI boom, who co-founded the American chipmaker and helped build it into the world’s second most valuable company.

In its first statement since reports emerged about Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns about U.S. national security and the future of the tech giant, Megaspeed said that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.”

U.S. intelligence agencies determined that Alice Huang had an affair with the Nvidia CEO and was a Chinese intelligence operative, a person with knowledge of the matter told NBC News on Sunday.

She held a senior position at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that was one of Nvidia’s biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed is under U.S. criminal investigation for allegedly smuggling American-made chips into China in defiance of U.S. export controls.

A criminal investigation is ongoing in Singapore, where officials said Thursday Alice Huang had been barred from re-entering the country. The government also issued her with a stern warning after finding that she had knowingly provided police with inaccurate information to downplay her role in the company. It said that Huang was not investigated for espionage.

The country’s Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement that authorities had interviewed Huang and impounded her passport in 2025, but that its requests for cooperation from U.S. authorities had gone unanswered.

“Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company,” it said.

Investigators concluded in February that there was “insufficient evidence to establish that Huang had committed any offences,” the statement said, adding that investigations into Megaspeed and six other individuals were continuing, related to the shipment of servers via Singapore.

Megaspeed, meanwhile, said in the statement Thursday that it has “cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and stands ready to cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority.” The statement was signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan.

It said that “Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government.”

China has dismissed the spying allegations as “smears.” On Thursday, a Foreign Ministry spokesperson said that “the U.S. side should stop fabricating so-called espionage narratives as a pretext for implementing technological blockades.”

Megaspeed did not address the allegations surrounding Alice Huang, but said that “to further reinforce our commitment to compliance, Megaspeed has retained a leading U.S. law firm to lead a comprehensive census of its graphics processing units (GPUs) and independently verify its export control compliance practices.”

The company added that it “welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws.”

Jensen Huang and Alice Huang in Taipei, Taiwan, in 2024.NetThunder

Nvidia’s stock price has plunged since its 63-year-old chief admitted over the weekend to being “unfaithful” to his wife.

Huang quit on Thursday in the wake of reports that he had multiple extramarital relationships. In a statement, Nvidia named its executive vice president and chief financial officer Colette Kress as its interim CEO.

Nvidia’s board met Wednesday night to address Huang’s future at the company, a source familiar with the matter told NBC News, adding that the White House was aware of the meeting.

The scandal has raised questions about how much U.S. government officials knew about Alice Huang and Megaspeed.

In the spring, Secretary of State Marco Rubio circulated a memo to officials in the Trump administration outlining how U.S. intelligence showed that the Nvidia CEO was in a romantic relationship with a business executive who was an asset of China’s spy service, according to a person familiar with Nvidia and a former national security official with knowledge of the matter. The New York Times and the Financial Times first reported on this memo.

Alice Huang’s precise role and relationship with China’s spy service remain unclear, however. It’s possible she was not a career spy for China’s spy agency, the Ministry of State Security, but was asked to cooperate and share information based on her access to Huang, a former national security official with knowledge of the matter told NBC News.

Rep. Jim Himes, D-Conn., ranking Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, told NPR that Alice Huang’s role still needed to be clarified.

Democrats will soon hold control of both the House and the Senate and, as a result, will have subpoena power.

On Wednesday night, as the Nvidia board met, Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Chris Coons, D-Del., announced they had written to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick with a request to preserve records on the subject.

The Board of Directors also appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever Chair of the Board.

Huang stepped down after he became embroiled in controversy over relationships with women at the company as well as with a customer who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. His departure is a serious blow to Nvidia, as he played a central role in positioning the chipmaker to become the market leader of the artificial intelligence boom at a time when competitors were unprepared for AI's rapid ascent.

Consequently, with Huang gone, Wall Street analysts slashed their share price targets. Nvidia's Nov. 17 earnings call remains the next major catalyst, and investors are watching whether management addresses leadership uncertainty and AI demand. h1.text: Nvidia Chief Seen as Target of Chinese Spy Plot

hl_nyt_1029.text:
TIMES EXCLUSIVE

Nvidia Chief Seen as Target of Chinese Spy Plot
Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, is influential at the White House on technology policy and has developed a close relationship with President Trump.

Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
SKIP TO CONTENT

A Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing. President Trump was briefed and took no action.

Listen · 16:14 min
Share full article1.1K

By Jonathan SwanMaggie HabermanAna SwansonPaul MozurTripp Mickle and Julian E. Barnes

Oct. 29, 2026
Leer en español阅读简体中文版閱讀繁體中文版

American spy agencies had gathered striking intelligence.

A top executive at a Singapore-based data center company was under scrutiny for possibly steering advanced Nvidia A.I. chips to China. And now American officials had concluded that she was a Chinese intelligence asset, funneling information to Beijing.

But what came next was even more alarming. Surveillance of the executive, Alice Huang or Huang Le, a Chinese citizen, revealed that she had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive.

For years, Washington has worked to deny China the technology needed to match or surpass the United States in the intense global competition for superiority in artificial intelligence. The discovery that Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access to Mr. Huang, one of the most powerful figures in the A.I. revolution as well as an influential ally of President Trump’s, set off alarms at the White House.

Roughly a year ago, Mr. Trump was briefed about the intelligence findings, which have not been previously reported, and chose not to do anything with the information. Mr. Trump has been wary of disrupting Nvidia’s chip sales, which are helping to drive the economy and the stock market, and of further complicating the trading relationship with China.

This account is based on interviews with people briefed on the surveillance, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because the findings are drawn from classified intelligence, as well as other officials and industry executives and analysts.

American officials already suspected that Ms. Huang was helping China evade constraints on its ability to gain access to advanced A.I. chips.

By Ana SwansonTripp MicklePaul Mozur and Mara Hvistendahl

Ana Swanson reported from Washington; Tripp Mickle from San Francisco and Fremont, Calif.; Paul Mozur from Taipei, Singapore and Johor, Malaysia; and Mara Hvistendahl from Amsterdam.

Oct. 9, 2025
阅读简体中文版閱讀繁體中文版

On a humid June night last year, Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, held court with several of his company’s major Asian customers at a bar with sweeping views of Taipei. They stood and toasted the booming artificial intelligence industry.

Next to the Nvidia chief was a woman named Huang Le, or Alice Huang, an executive of a Singapore-based data center company called Megaspeed, which was poised to buy $2 billion of Nvidia A.I. technology over the next year.

Though Ms. Huang and Megaspeed are little-known players in the A.I. industry, their association with Nvidia and its chief executive has recently become a preoccupation in Washington.

Commerce Department officials have been investigating whether Megaspeed, which has close ties to Chinese tech firms, is helping companies in China sidestep American export restrictions, according to more than a half dozen current and former officials and other people familiar with the companies, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss an examination that is not public.

ADVERTISEMENT

SKIP ADVERTISEMENT

The inquiry, which is active, calls into question how closely Nvidia is tracking where its A.I. chips end up and highlights the possibility of American export laws easily being sidestepped. Megaspeed is also facing scrutiny from Singaporean police, who told The New York Times in a statement that they are investigating the company for breaching local laws, without elaborating further.

As the dominant provider of artificial intelligence chips, Nvidia’s annual revenue has soared nearly sevenfold in the past four years, making it the world’s most valuable publicly traded company. But the Silicon Valley company’s meteoric rise has coincided with U.S. government concerns that its chips could help adversaries like China develop new weapons, surveil dissidents and leap ahead of the United States in A.I. development.

By Maureen Farrell and Rob Copeland

Nov. 13, 2026
See more of our coverage in your search results.
Add The New York Times as a preferred source on Google›

With Jensen Huang’s abrupt ouster from Nvidia, Wall Street has lost its most powerful and profitable dealmaker.

As Mr. Huang built Nvidia from a regional chipmaker into the world’s largest company, he dispensed with the usual careful, corporate hand-wringing. He personally directed splashy deals and complicated financing structures that pumped hundreds of billions of dollars into would-be competitors, suppliers and customers.

If that made him, in the public eye, a face of the global A.I. build out, on Wall Street he represented something else: manna. His deals produced billions of dollars in fees for banks, asset managers and advisers, and Nvidia was, up until this week, spending or promising money at a speed and magnitude of little precedence.

Now Wall Street bankers, traders and even some of Nvidia’s competitors are wondering and worrying about whether Mr. Huang’s departure will slow the breakneck pace of Nvidia’s investments.

ADVERTISEMENT

Some say that the fundamentals of Nvidia’s power are still intact, like its extreme control of the global supply of chips, the A.I. boom’s scarcest resource, the company’s deep cash coffers and the Trump administration’s warm support for the industry’s regulatory agenda. But Mr. Huang was the leader who harnessed all of those assets into a deal-making machine.

“Nvidia is the central bank of A.I.,” said Michael Edwards, director of Forum Markets, an A.I.-focused merchant bank. “Imagine the Fed without a chairman.”

The resignation of Jensen Huang capped a stunning downfall for one of the most pivotal players in the artificial intelligence boom.

Mr. Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive on Thursday following revelations that he had affairs with an executive who reported to him and with a woman who United States officials believe was spying for China.

Nvidia Chief Seen as Target of Chinese Spy Plot

A Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing. President Trump was briefed and took no action.

Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, is influential at the White House on technology policy and has developed a close relationship with President Trump.

American spy agencies had gathered striking intelligence.

A top executive at a Singapore-based data center company was under scrutiny for possibly steering advanced Nvidia A.I. chips to China. And now American officials had concluded that she was a Chinese intelligence asset, funneling information to Beijing.

But what came next was even more alarming. Surveillance of the executive, Alice Huang or Huang Le, a Chinese citizen, revealed that she had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive.

For years, Washington has worked to deny China the technology needed to match or surpass the United States in the intense global competition for superiority in artificial intelligence. The discovery that Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access to Mr. Huang, one of the most powerful figures in the A.I. revolution as well as an influential ally of President Trump’s, set off alarms at the White House.

Roughly a year ago, Mr. Trump was briefed about the intelligence findings, which have not been previously reported, and chose not to do anything with the information. Mr. Trump has been wary of disrupting Nvidia’s chip sales, which are helping to drive the economy and the stock market, and of further complicating the trading relationship with China.

By Eric Revell FOXBusiness
Nvidia shares dive after CEO Jensen Huang resigns

Fox News contributor Michael Pillsbury discusses the resignation of Nividia CEO Jensen Huang and the long-term controversy with U.S. policy in China.

The abrupt resignation of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia Thursday following reports he engaged in multiple extramarital affairs leaves the AI giant facing an uncertain future, and a longtime company executive is stepping in as interim CEO.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as its CEO until his resignation, transforming the company from a struggling startup into one of the world's largest by market capitalization amid surging demand for its AI chips. He became a visionary and figurehead for the AI revolution.

Nvidia Chief Financial Officer and EVP Colette Kress has been named the company's interim CEO after serving as Nvidia's CFO since September 2013. 

NVIDIA LOSES ITS 'GODFATHER OF AI' AND NOW FACES FIRST BIG TEST WITHOUT HIM

She has deep experience in tech finance, previously working as a CFO for Cisco's business technology and operations finance unit and was also CFO of Microsoft's server and tools division during a 13-year tenure at the software giant.

Analysts view Kress, who has featured prominently in Nvidia's quarterly earnings calls, as a steady hand who can help the company navigate a tumultuous period after the departure of its longtime leader.

Nvidia named chief financial officer Colette Kress as the company's interim CEO following Huang's resignation. (Nvidia/Handout / Reuters)

Bret Kenwell, U.S. investment analyst at eToro, said that while "Huang was more than a CEO and part of the investment thesis," the selection of longtime Nvidia executive Kress as interim CEO should "provide stability and reassurance" to investors.

"Kress has been a familiar presence at Nvidia and on its conference calls, offering a recognizable voice during an already fragile situation," Kenwell added.

Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly earnings Tuesday, Nov. 17, which will give Kress an early opportunity to assuage investors' concerns.

"We always believed she would eventually be CEO of a major public tech company, but she would have to leave Nvidia after many years there," Ives added.

TRUMP SAYS 'THERE IS ONLY ONE MAN' TO REPLACE JENSEN HUANG AS NVIDIA CEO

Nvidia became the preeminent company in the AI space under Huang's leadership and is one of the largest companies in the world by market cap. (Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images)

Huang's departure will pose other challenges for Nvidia and Kress given the level of visibility he brought to Nvidia's AI business and his ability to broker deals around the world.

Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said Kress will be viewed as a "safe pair of hands" who has "been brought into steady leadership, but she lacks global status."

Streeter added that Kress is "unlikely to be able to forge such deep commercial ties, and Nvidia will now enter this period of uncertainty over strategic priorities, pricing and supply agreements."

NVIDIA'S JENSEN HUANG REGIME CHANGE A WARNING TO COMPANIES AND INVESTORS EVERYWHERE, BUSINESS EXPERT CAUTIONS

Jensen Huang served as Nvidia CEO from the time he co-founded the company in 1993 until his resignation on Nov. 12, 2026. (Reuters/Kylie Cooper)

Michael Landsberg, chief investment officer at Landsberg Bennett Private Wealth Management, said Huang's resignation "is the worst-case scenario during this entire saga."

"He was not just a leader, but a visionary for the company, and while CFO Colette Kress is highly capable and respected, there are still big questions about how the innovation of Nvidia will evolve without Jensen."

Gil Luria, managing director at DA Davidson, said "Kress is well respected by investors and should be able to guide Nvidia through this challenging period."

Ex-NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang is set to testify before Congress this month

House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast said the hearing will take place before Thanksgiving.

by
 
Kris Holt
Nov. 12, 2026 12:53 pm EST
Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images
Add Engadget on Google:
